subject: Urgent: Production stalls — batch lane starvation and cache feedback loop
messages:

Date: 2026-08-16T15:12:00Z
Subject: Important — request stalls and 500s on inference in US region

Hi Monica / Vivek,

Starting around 14:50 UTC we saw a spike of 5xx errors and a large fraction of requests that appear to be 'stalled' (client timers show requests hanging ~5–10s before a 500). P99 latency for our flows jumped from ~220ms to >3s. This is affecting our order-routing pipeline and causing retries.

Attached a short sample of logs (service-log-20260816.txt) and the request IDs for a few stalled requests: 9a3b, 9a3c, 9a7f. Can someone confirm whether this is on your side or if we should scale down traffic? We are on the Dedicated pool in us-west-2.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T15:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Important — request stalls and 500s on inference in US region

Quick technical summary from infra:
- Symptom: lanes in our batching scheduler are experiencing starvation when a mix of high-concurrency short-prefix requests and a small number of long-sequence requests arrive together. The scheduler's lane heuristics are sending too many requests into the same GPU worker which then thrashes the KV cache.
- Observed cascade: KV cache ephemeral evictions -> more cache misses -> longer service times -> scheduler queues more requests into same worker due to affinity heuristics -> increased P99 and 500s. It's a feedback loop.
- Evidence: runtime profiles show 43% increase in cache miss rate for Atlas workloads starting at 14:47 UTC and sustained queue depth spikes on worker-23. See attached profiler snapshot.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short window):
1) Reduce max_batch_wait from 25ms -> 10ms for Atlas routing policy (reduces lane accumulation).
2) Increase KV cache soft quota for Atlas from 12GB -> 18GB for the next 2 hours (falls back after).
3) Temporarily disable aggressive affinity-based batching for requests tagged as low-prefix-length (to avoid hot-lane concentration).

I'll prepare a runbook for the above. If we need to act now I can push the batch_wait change as a hot-config.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

Jordan — immediate mitigations executed at 16:15 UTC:
- Reduced max_batch_wait for your routing policy to 10ms.
- Increased KV cache soft quota by ~50% for the dedicated pool (temporary, monitored).
- Disabled aggressive affinity batching for low-prefix flows.

Early results: p99 dropped from ~3s -> ~400ms and 5xx rate decreased by ~78% in the first 10 minutes. We're continuing to monitor; no further client throttling requested at this time.

Next steps (we will follow up in writing):
- Post-incident root cause analysis and proposed changes to batching lane heuristics.
- Consider quota/eviction policy changes for dedicated pools to reduce susceptibility to cache-feedback loops.
- Alignment call with Atlas in the next 24 hours to review impact and credits if any.

Apologies again for the hit — we take this seriously. I've attached a short mitigation-plan-draft.md for your review.

—Monica
